ABB Ltd Reports Steady Trade Figures Amid Stable Market Conditions

Zurich—ABB Ltd, a leading player in Switzerland’s electrical equipment sector, reported routine trade figures for the latest quarter, highlighting a period of stable demand and consistent performance in both domestic and international markets. The company’s latest data show that order volumes and shipment levels have remained broadly in line with last year’s corresponding period, reflecting steady activity across its core segments.

According to figures released on Thursday, ABB Ltd posted total exports valued at CHF 1.42 billion for the quarter ending in May, a marginal 1.1% increase compared to the same period last year. Imports for the quarter stood at CHF 1.35 billion, marking a 0.8% rise year-on-year. Company officials described the results as “in keeping with expectations,” citing balanced order books and sustained customer demand from energy, infrastructure, and industrial automation sectors.

“The figures confirm the resilience of our business model and the trust our partners place in our solutions,” said Martina Keller, ABB’s Chief Financial Officer. “We continue to see healthy demand in Switzerland and across our main export destinations, particularly within the European Union and select Asian markets.”

Industry analysts noted that ABB Ltd’s performance reflects broader trends in the electrical equipment industry, which has seen consistent but unspectacular growth in recent quarters. “With supply chains largely normalized and input costs stabilizing, companies like ABB are well-positioned to maintain reliable delivery and service levels,” commented Felix Brunner, an analyst at the Swiss Industrial Trade Institute.

Trade data shows that orders for power grid components and automation systems remained robust, while demand for building electrification products recorded a slight uptick, supported by ongoing infrastructure investments in both public and private sectors. Domestic demand continued to be buoyed by energy efficiency initiatives and upgrades to municipal power networks.

The Swiss Association of Electrical Manufacturers welcomed the figures, describing them as “a sign of continued market confidence and operational stability.” Labor representatives from the National Electrical Workers’ Union echoed this sentiment, noting the absence of any major disruptions or labor issues during the reporting period.

ABB Ltd’s next scheduled financial update is expected later this summer, with executives expressing cautious optimism for continued steady performance.
